newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasoline holds gains after refinery rumor.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasoline holds gains after refinery rumor.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices held gains while distillates fell in late Friday trade, after rumors surfaced of a refinery problem in San Francisco and a change in military jet fuel suppliers.
Middle distillates were forecast to fall next week on rumors that the military changed who it granted jet fuel contracts.
"There seems to be a major shift in who'se got jet and who doesn't," a West Coast broker said.
A key Los Angeles refinery was rumored to be balanced in product rather than long, after it allegedly won a contract.
But the supply situations seemed unclear, forcing sellers to trim a half cent for jet fuel in L.A., hitting 72.50 cents a gallon.
Low sulphur, or "EPA" diesel, pared early gains by falling 1.50 cents to 70/71 cents a gallon. Traders speculated that demand was soft ahead of heavy oxygenate blending season.
Meanwhile, NYMEX unleaded gasoline ended the week by rising 1.61 cents a gallon to 64.60 cents a gallon, ahead of Monday's expiry.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles flattened at 72.00/72.50.
Wholesale prices for conventional regular gasoline in Los Angeles stayed 66/67 cents a gallon.
Earlier, San Francisco gasolines tightened their differential off Los Angeles grades to one cent, on unconfirmed but widely heard reports of a Bay-area refinery problem.
